title: Hosted API Demo: Chat/Text Generation Basics
summary: AE + SE walkthrough of Redwood hosted API focusing on chat/text generation basics: streaming, key params (temperature, max_tokens, top_p), retry/backoff guidance, and next steps to run a short benchmark. Customer interested in latency and cost tradeoffs for interactive product use case.
next_steps: Ava to send hosted API pricing + rate limit doc by 2025-06-20
Kenji to share basic benchmark script and retry examples by 2025-06-21
Schedule 30m POC scoping call (customer requested week of 6/30)

Kenji Sato | Provide python/curl retry examples and small benchmark script | 2025-06-21
Tom Li | Confirm POC scope and internal stakeholders for week of 6/30 | 2025-06-23
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-06-18 15:00 PDT | Duration 42m | Attendees: Ava (Redwood AE), Kenji (Redwood SE), Tom (NovaPay), Priya (NovaPay), Michael (NovaPay)

[00:00] Ava (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. uh quick intro from our side, I’m Ava, AE on the Redwood hosted team. Kenji will do most of the demo and go into SDKs and streaming.
[00:10] Tom (NovaPay): Thanks AvA, Tom here, Head of Eng at NovaPay. We build payment UXs that have chat assistants embedded in the dashboard so latency matters a lot.
[00:18] Priya (NovaPay): Hey all, Priya, ML eng, will be running evals. we care about cost and ensuring model outputs are controlled.
[00:25] Kenji (Redwood SE): Cool, thanks. quick agenda: 1) quick API walkthrough for chat/text, 2) streaming demo, 3) retry/params guidance and 4) Q+A + next steps.
[00:36] Kenji (Redwood SE): I’ll start with the request shape. For chat we take messages array, role/content, you can call the /v1/chat/completions endpoint or the unified /v1/generate for text. Example payload: {"model":"redwood-hosted-1","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Summarize this..."}],"temperature":0.2,"max_tokens":150}. (note: auto-transcription replaced braces sometimes)
[01:05] Priya (NovaPay): Quick q — do you support streaming tokens back? we need partial responses to render typing indicator.
[01:12] Kenji (Redwood SE): yes, streaming supported. we stream via chunked responses over the same endpoint, or via our SDKs that expose an on_token callback. latency is typically dominated by first-token generation and network; our console shows token level timing.
[01:30] Ava (Redwood AE): For production we recommend streaming + a small initial token budget so UI can display quickly while later tokens fill in.
[01:40] Michael (NovaPay): Any limits? how many concurrent streams can we run — we have interactive flows with 500 active users during spikes.
[01:48] Kenji (Redwood SE): Concurrency depends on plan. Hosted has per-account quotas and rate limits; for spikes you can request burst capacity or move to Dedicated. We’ll include explicit numbers in the pricing doc.
[02:05] Kenji (Redwood SE): Now demo: I’ll call from python using the SDK. (typing, demo audio)
[02:18] Kenji (Redwood SE): Example code: client = RedwoodClient(api_key=...); stream = client.chat.stream(model="redwood-chat-medium", messages=...); for token in stream: print(token) — shows on_token handler. We also showed curl: curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" -d '{"model":"...","messages":[...],"stream":true}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat.
[03:00] Tom (NovaPay): had an issue with other vendors where streaming dropped mid-response — how do you recommend handling reconnects?
[03:10] Kenji (Redwood SE): Good q. We recommend idempotent request ids and edge retries with exponential backoff. If a stream drops after N tokens, the client can re-issue a request with the same conversation state and request_id and the server will continue from last committed token; we also provide a token-offset in the stream metadata (note: sometimes metadata label in transcript is wrong).
[03:40] Priya (NovaPay): That sounds ideal. any built-in dedupe for at-least-once semantics?
[03:45] Kenji (Redwood SE): We provide idempotency keys and recommend the client keep the last message or last token index. There’s still nuance if you have function-calling side effects — transactional steps should be behind a separate guaranteed delivery channel.
[04:10] Ava (Redwood AE): Outline of tuning params: temperature (0.0-1.0) controls randomness; for deterministic summaries pick 0.0-0.2; for creative copy 0.7+. max_tokens sets output length; top_p and frequency_penalty available. Default batching and KV cache optimizations reduce cost for repeated prefixes.
[04:47] Tom (NovaPay): For our ui, we prefer shorter, constrained replies — likely max_tokens 100 and temperature 0.2.
[04:55] Kenji (Redwood SE): Great. we also have streaming partials + stop tokens to avoid trailing fragments. you can pass stop sequences in the request.
[05:12] Kenji (Redwood SE): Now retries and HTTP semantics: use 429/503 handling with exponential backoff jitter, we suggest 500ms x (2^attempt) up to a cap, then alert. For idempotent calls include X-Request-ID header. For non-idempotent (function calls) we recommend queuing at app layer.
[05:40] Priya (NovaPay): do you expose request logs in the console? helpful for debugging retries/errors.
[05:45] Ava (Redwood AE): yes, Console shows per-request traces, latency per-token, and cost breakdown. you can filter by request_id and export logs for audits.
[06:00] Michael (NovaPay): security — how are keys rotated? we need KMS integration.
[06:07] Kenji (Redwood SE): Hosted supports customer-managed keys via KMS for enterprise, audit logs, SSO, RBAC. For the hosted tier we offer encrypted-at-rest and optional BYOK for Private. We’ll attach SOC2 doc in the follow up. (customer asked for SOC2 earlier)
[06:30] Kenji (Redwood SE): Quick live test: I’m going to send a prompt that streams a short summary, watch tokens come in. (demo: streaming shown, occasional network hiccup simulated)
[07:05] Ava (Redwood AE): you can see on the console the tokens per second and cumulative cost estimate.
[07:18] Tom (NovaPay): question — what about retrying only on idempotent ops, but if we do end up resending a non-idempotent call like a payment webhook, how do you suggest avoiding duplicates?
[07:28] Kenji (Redwood SE): handle side effects outside of the LLM call; have the LLM return a structured payload and then your system performs actions once it validates; or use a transaction log with dedupe keys. We have customers that write small validation services between the model and their payments processor.
[08:00] Priya (NovaPay): any tuning recommendations for cost? we have a bursty but small average qps.
[08:07] Kenji (Redwood SE): Use quantized model variants, prefix caching for repeated system prompts, and batching for background tasks; for interactive flows streaming + smaller max_tokens helps. Our Optimize product can suggest batching and quantization profiles based on traces.
[08:30] Tom (NovaPay): do you do auto-fallback to cheaper models if latency increases?
[08:36] Kenji (Redwood SE): Yes, smart routing can fallback by policy to compatible model variants. You can configure latency SLO and cost thresholds per-route.
[08:55] Ava (Redwood AE): showing Console now — route config, per-model dashboards, trace view. (screen share) you can see an example route with canary and automatic rollback.
[09:30] Michael (NovaPay): demo looks good. any sample benchmarks we can run ourselves?
[09:38] Kenji (Redwood SE): I’ll share a small script that runs a 1k sample with concurrency and measures p50/p95 latency and tokens/sec; it includes retry backoff config.
[10:00] Tom (NovaPay): ok let's talk about integration timeline — our Q3 launch target. we need a POC to validate latency at scale and compliance review.
[10:11] Ava (Redwood AE): sounds good. typical POC is 2-4 weeks: run benchmarks, integrate SDK, run security review (we’ll provide SOC2 and architecture review), then decide on Hosted vs Dedicated.
[10:28] Priya (NovaPay): for POC, can we spin up a limited dedicated pool? or will hosted suffice?
[10:34] Kenji (Redwood SE): Usually hosted suffices for initial POC; if you need guaranteed throughput we can provision a temporary dedicated pool for the pilot — that requires contract ops but doable.
[11:00] Tom (NovaPay): what are typical costs per 1k tokens?
[11:05] Ava (Redwood AE): we’ll include typical per-token pricing and a cost model in the doc; pricing varies by model size and quantization.
[11:20] (transcript contains some mis-hearings) Speaker 2: yeah uh the token pricing um is model dependent, apologies if that was fuzzy.
[11:40] Kenji (Redwood SE): more on retries: we suggested pattern: initial quick retry short window for transient network errors, then exponential backoff for 429/503, log to console, and alert if repeated. Also include client side circuit breaker to avoid thrashing.
[12:10] Priya (NovaPay): do you provide client libraries that implement these retries?
[12:15] Kenji (Redwood SE): Yes, official SDKs include a retry policy you can configure and examples in python/js. We’ll attach the code snippet.
[12:40] Tom (NovaPay): any rate limit headers returned? can we inspect headers for remaining quota?
[12:45] Kenji (Redwood SE): yes we provide X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, and backoff windows in headers.
[13:00] Ava (Redwood AE): let’s address a few edge cases: long-running generation — you can stream and checkpoint partial outputs to resume; also you can use KV cache for chat context to reduce compute for repeated prefixes.
[13:25] Michael (NovaPay): KV cache — is that something we control?
[13:29] Kenji (Redwood SE): It’s managed by our runtime; you can configure cache TTL and pin system prompts. For Private deployments customers can host KV cache locally.
[13:50] Priya (NovaPay): do you support structured output or function calling?
[13:55] Kenji (Redwood SE): yes we support structured JSON responses and function calling semantics; best practice is to validate and schema-check responses before executing.
[14:10] Tom (NovaPay): ok good. back to streaming — any gotchas for mobile clients?
[14:16] Kenji (Redwood SE): Mobile can keep a websocket/long-poll to receive streams; consider network drops, use small chunk sizes and rehydration with request_id. Also consider charging for bytes vs tokens if on metered mobile networks.
[14:40] Ava (Redwood AE): we’ll follow up with the security pack and the SOC2 report.
[14:45] Kenji (Redwood SE): I’ll drop the benchmark script in the repo and the retry + streaming examples.
[15:00] Tom (NovaPay): great, that answers a lot. can you add a suggested configuration for p50 target of 300ms first-token?
[15:08] Kenji (Redwood SE): yes we’ll suggest model variant and routing rules to help meet that SLO; note that hosted first-token 300ms depends on region and model size.
[15:25] Ava (Redwood AE): recap and next steps: 1) we’ll send pricing and rate limit doc, 2) Kenji will share benchmark script and code examples, 3) customer to confirm POC stakeholders and timeline.
[15:40] Michael (NovaPay): thanks everyone. we’ll review and aim to have internal stakeholder list by next week.
[15:50] — End of recorded transcript (transcription quality medium; some small mis-hearings and punctuation errors).

Notes: references shared during call: link: https://redwood.example/pricing (placeholder), link: https://redwood.example/soc2, repo: github.com/redwood/benchmarks (placeholder).
